research_mode: official ONS latest crime bulletin only; survey, police-recorded, knife, firearm, fraud-transition and comparability gates; no parcel, exact-location, candidate or business result claimed

sources.name: Latest crime bulletin release
verified_claims: Crime in England and Wales: year ending March 2026 was released on 23 July 2026 as the latest bulletin.
limitations: Publication recency does not make every component dataset equally current.

sources.name: CSEW household population scope
verified_claims: The CSEW is a face-to-face survey of people aged 16 years and over who are resident in households.
limitations: Survey estimates must not be assigned to people or properties outside the sampled population.

sources.name: CSEW excluded populations
verified_claims: The CSEW excludes businesses, public-sector bodies, tourists and people living in communal establishments such as prisons and care homes.
limitations: CSEW estimates are not complete measures for all populations or premises.

sources.name: Incident and prevalence measures
verified_claims: CSEW headline crime is reported as estimated incident counts and victim prevalence.
limitations: Incident counts and victim prevalence are different measures and must not be interchanged.

sources.name: Separate self-completion measures
verified_claims: Domestic abuse, sexual victimisation and stalking are collected separately from headline crime, mainly through privacy-protecting self-completion questions.
limitations: These prevalence measures must not be added directly to headline-crime incident totals.

sources.name: Sexual-victimisation redevelopment break
verified_claims: Sexual-victimisation questions were redeveloped and the latest estimates are not comparable with previously published measures.
limitations: A year-on-year trend must not be calculated across the measurement break.

sources.name: Domestic-abuse and stalking publication delay
verified_claims: Year ending March 2026 domestic-abuse and stalking estimates are scheduled for later publication after additional quality assurance.
limitations: Their absence from the July bulletin must not be represented as zero prevalence.

sources.name: Police-recorded wider scope
verified_claims: Police-recorded crime covers wider populations and offences, including children, institutions, tourists, businesses and crimes against society.
limitations: It includes only notifiable offences reported to and recorded by police.

sources.name: Police-recorded trend limitation
verified_claims: Changes in police activity and recording practices make police-recorded crime a better indicator of police activity than general crime trends.
limitations: Recorded-volume changes must not automatically be treated as prevalence changes.

sources.name: Report Fraud transition
verified_claims: Report Fraud launched in December 2025 to replace Action Fraud and the National Fraud Intelligence Bureau systems.
limitations: System transition creates a break in recorded fraud-data supply.

sources.name: Recorded fraud temporary omission
verified_claims: Recorded cybercrime and fraud data are not presented while the City of London Police transitions systems and aligns legacy data.
limitations: The omission must not be interpreted as no fraud or cybercrime.

sources.name: CSEW fraud continuity
verified_claims: CSEW fraud and computer-misuse estimates are unaffected by the recorded-data system transition.
limitations: Survey fraud estimates and police-recorded fraud are different measures.

sources.name: Preferred source by crime type
verified_claims: ONS prefers CSEW for broad victimisation trends and police data for homicide, weapon offences and robbery.
limitations: Source choice must follow offence coverage rather than use one source for all crime types.

sources.name: Headline crime estimate
verified_claims: The CSEW estimated 9.6 million headline-crime incidents with no statistically significant change from the previous survey year.
limitations: The national estimate does not provide parcel or exact-address counts.

sources.name: Police-recorded homicide 2026
verified_claims: Police recorded 499 homicide offences in the year ending March 2026, 7% fewer than the previous year.
limitations: Headline police homicide figures differ from Homicide Index figures.

sources.name: Homicide collection distinction
verified_claims: Police-recorded homicide and Homicide Index figures are not directly comparable because the index incorporates court outcomes and more detailed information.
limitations: The two collections require separate source labels and snapshot dates.

sources.name: Knife-enabled crime definition
verified_claims: Knife-enabled crime includes use to injure, attempt to injure or threaten, including cases where the weapon was believed present but not seen.
limitations: The category does not prove weapon recovery or exact weapon type in every offence.

sources.name: Knife-enabled offence total
verified_claims: Police-recorded knife-enabled crime decreased by 8% to 48,774 offences in the year ending March 2026.
limitations: The national total must not be allocated to parcels without validated spatial records.

sources.name: Knife methodology transition
verified_claims: By March 2026, 41 police forces had switched to the National Data Quality Improvement Service method for identifying knife-enabled offences.
limitations: Force and time comparisons must account for methodology transition.

sources.name: Knife-enabled offence composition
verified_claims: Assault categories represented 44% and robbery 39% of knife-enabled crime, while homicide represented less than 1%.
limitations: Offence composition does not identify the circumstances or exact location of an individual case.
